experiment_kind: Unvalidated method-reproduction experiment restoring historical foothold behavior on pinned modern author code; not a certified original 2024 release.

mpc.control_parameterization: one historical cubic segment, four knots per force, 48 total parameters

failure.description: Native gym_quadruped invalid non-leg/foot ground contact; no added roll/pitch or height cutoff

video.selection: all fig4; seed 0 and lowest-index failed and successful table1 episodes for each method, without cutting

implementation_choices: Use the pinned modern author code c46cb9a3960554cffc467a71c6674b65c0f4a2c8 with the dated gym-quadruped Aliengo model efb7217b9515613b238405846dcdbc92cf07f488 and explicit source patches. This is a configured, not yet validated baseline candidate; neither snapshot is certified as the exact original paper release.

Relative to r1-v7-paper-model, restore two documented foothold behaviors from historical author source 5c763068126499255c5e80898999aa83f3226ff8: lateral hip-to-foot offset 0.1 m per side instead of 0.083 m, and world-frame lift-off points fixed throughout each swing instead of moving with the body. Preserve the modern API; do not claim that these changes restore the entire 2024 control chain or have already improved results.
Keep phase_consistent_swing=false, as in r1-v7-paper-model. The separate swing-clock repair is not combined with the foothold restoration, so its effect is not attributed to these two changes.

The fixed naive and adaptive author controllers use different force-spline time parameterizations. Add adaptive_fixed using the same adaptive controller implementation, cost, sampling, and low-level execution as adaptive, while restricting candidate frequency to [1.3] Hz. Compare adaptive_fixed against adaptive to isolate the benefit of permitting frequency optimization; preserve naive for the paper-style comparison.

Paper omits numerical Q/R/covariance. Use historical sampling Q, sigma, and one-segment cubic interpolation; nominal acados retains its different author Q/R. Compare common physical task metrics rather than treating different optimizer costs as equivalent.

The historical and modern naive samplers use two Gaussians plus a uniform component at fixed scales, retaining the previous mean as a candidate. Preserve the actual author implementation and disclose its difference from the paper description of multiple Gaussian distributions.

Enable the sampling input-force cost specified in the paper, using nominal acados force weights 0.001 and masking nominal stance load on swing legs. Historical and modern sampling source comment out this term; its inclusion is a paper-method reimplementation choice, not literal historical-code reproduction.

Use absolute MPPI lambda=1 without cost-spread normalization. Disable OT-MPC, gradient refinement, Riccati feedback, foothold optimization, integrators, external wrench compensation, reflexes, velocity modulation, and friction compensation.

Use historical SciPy cubic swing, gains 5000/100, step height 0.3*hip_height, velocity averaging, and 5 cm velocity-error correction clipping. Preserve modern CoM-based SRBD state and corresponding base-height reference adjustment; historical source used base position. Modern initial gait phase is fixed rather than the historical random global phase.

Adaptive prediction starts at the actual current contact phase; frequency decisions occur at swing apex. These explicit phase-consistency choices remain distinct from certification of an original paper snapshot.

Paper states 21 kg, while dated and modern author models are approximately 24.638 kg. Use the actual MJCF mass and initial-pose inertia consistently in all controllers. The dated model retains its damping, friction, armature, torque limits, contact options, and home pose; the massless foot-body adapter only supports the modern feet-position API.

Figure 4 uses the explicitly declared world-frame velocity [0, 0.1, 0] m/s and world-y 40 N from 2 to 5 s. The paper gives inconsistent push durations and does not fully specify the forward command despite showing forward displacement; this is a declared push-response reconstruction, not a certified identical trajectory.

Table I omits episode duration, command, complete wrench schedule, and failure threshold. Use 60 s, the Figure 3 forward command, 2 s wrench holds, and native gym-quadruped invalid-contact termination. All four methods use the same 50 disturbance seeds. Do not tune these conditions to force the published success percentages; the reported 37 percent also cannot correspond exactly to 50 integer Bernoulli outcomes.

Paper Mean Cost/tracking-error scalar is not fully defined. Retain linear-velocity error norm, RMSE, common quadratic state/input metrics, task duration, and all success/failure outcomes separately. Do not equate lower error on a prematurely terminated episode with better full-task performance.

Separate first-solve JIT compilation from steady-state solve time while retaining it in raw trajectories. Actual hardware, command, source/configuration versions, and output paths must accompany new runs; no previous trajectory is relabeled as the restored-foothold condition.
